+def _reindex_and_align_datasets(datasets, join, fill_value):
+    """
+    Reindex datasets to have the same variables.
+    
+    When join='outer', missing variables are filled with fill_value.
+    When join='inner', only variables present in all datasets are kept.
+    """
+    from .dataset import Dataset
+    
+    if join == 'inner':
+        # Only keep variables present in all datasets
+        all_vars = set(datasets[0].variables)
+        for ds in datasets[1:]:
+            all_vars = all_vars & set(ds.variables)
+        
+        # Reindex each dataset to only have common variables
+        datasets = [ds[list(all_vars)] for ds in datasets]
+    elif join == 'outer':
+        # Collect all variables from all datasets
+        all_vars = set()
+        for ds in datasets:
+            all_vars = all_vars | set(ds.variables)
+        
+        # For each dataset, add missing variables filled with fill_value
+        new_datasets = []
+        for ds in datasets:
+            missing_vars = all_vars - set(ds.variables)
+            if missing_vars:
+                # Create dummy variables for missing ones
+                new_vars = {}
+                for var in missing_vars:
+                    # Find the variable in another dataset to get its dimensions and dtype
+                    for other_ds in datasets:
+                        if var in other_ds.variables:
+                            other_var = other_ds.variables[var]
+                            # Create a dummy variable with fill_value
+                            import numpy as np
+                            shape = tuple(ds.dims.get(d, 1) for d in other_var.dims)
+                            # Use float64 for NaN values
+                            data = np.full(shape, fill_value, dtype=np.float64)
+                            new_vars[var] = Variable(other_var.dims, data)
+                            break
+                
+                # Create a new dataset with the added variables
+                ds = ds.copy()
+                for var, val in new_vars.items():
+                    ds[var] = val
+            
+            new_datasets.append(ds)
+        
+        datasets = new_datasets
+    
+    return datasets
+
